heroHeadline: Drone Crisis Passes a Dozen Breaches Hours Before Russia Opens Contested Duma Voting in Transnistria
heroSubtitle: Moldova's airspace has now been breached thirteen times since the drone crisis began August 9, with four new crossings since September 8: a Shahed-type drone that delayed President Zelensky's flight from Chisinau on September 8 was confirmed to be a newer, faster-flying Geran-4 variant; a drone transited Moldova into Romania's Suceava County on September 12; two drones crossed near Palanca and Ciuburciu in a single morning on September 14; and another crossed near Tudora on September 17, hours before Russia's disputed plan to open polling stations across Transnistria for the September 18-20 State Duma election — 17 planned against the single station Chisinau has authorised. Separately, Hungary on September 9 declined to extend its veto of Ukraine's EU accession cluster to Moldova, opening a possible path to decouple the two candidates' long-linked cluster track, while Energy Minister Dorin Junghietu said on September 10 that Moldova will not return to its old Gazprom-supplied gas model and has told Transnistria to build its own reserves.
footerNote: Data sourced from official reports, major outlets, and institutional analyses.
